notes:
**A price alert crossed while the app was shut never arrived.** Alerts only fired on a crossing a running app watched happen. Set one above the price, close the app, let the market pass the level overnight, open it in the morning - nothing. And that is the commonest case, because people set an alert precisely so they do not have to watch. An alert now remembers which side the price was on when you set it, and that answers on the first tick after a launch.

**Your backtests keep their history, and keep it tidy.** The candle archive is wired in: whatever depth your broker grants is stored on the phone, so a window it refuses today is still there if it was served last week. It stores only what is new or corrected, so running the same backtest fifty times does not grow the file - and it fills the window you asked for rather than quietly widening it.
